column1: > Every file the Linux and macOS packages install, and where it lands.

column3: where it lands, relative to the person's home directory. On macOS
that is the payload tree pkgbuild is handed; on Linux it is the
tree install.sh copies out of the tarball.
gobuild    go build the package at <from> in <source>, unless --bin
names a directory that already holds the built programs
copy       take the file at <from> out of <source>
authored   written here, in installer/posix/, and shipped as it stands
license    the file --license names; <source> is posix and <from> is "-".
The one LICENSE at a repository root is the whole obligation,
and which root that is depends on which repository is being
built, so it is an argument rather than a source id

column2: an id from sources.tsv, or "posix" for a file that lives here

column1: > The Panel is not here: it has no publishable source on any platform, and it is
> a Windows program. The C++ header is not here either — bindings/download-over-curl
> publishes from nowhere. The Windows package gates both away and says so; these
> two do not carry the rows at all, and the release notes name both.
> @BIN@ in an authored file is the absolute directory the three programs land in.
> install.sh on Linux and scripts/postinstall on macOS substitute it. Nothing
> else is substituted at install time anywhere.
> A source with no --src has its rows left out of the package and each one named,
> the way the Windows build gates the UNRESOLVED rows. A program is never left
> out that way: a gobuild row with neither --src nor --bin stops the build. That
> is what lets a package built only from published module versions ship the three
> programs without checking out the repositories the Python files come from -
> those are published on their own registry, and a redistributable carrying a
> second copy of them would be one file with two homes.
